summary.intent: Autonomously run the full GSD ship-phase loop (verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit → ship → resolve PR reviews) for phase 73 of the cipher-box repo, without user babysitting.
summary.outcome: All gates passed (verify 7/7, secure 17/17 threats closed, crypto/privacy clean, security-review clean, validate 0 gaps, SDK E2E 106/106 after fixing a stale test contract, CodeRabbit CLI 0 findings after fixing a MAJOR); PR #603 was opened with CI all green, and the assistant was mid-way through triaging/fixing CodeRabbit + Greptile PR-level review findings (one real fix applied to client.ts, one todo logged, two false positives dismissed) when the transcript ends.

repo: cipher-box commit subjects for phase 73 were already conventional (`fix(73-08):`, `test(73-01):`), so the standard 'reword non-conventional GSD executor commits via filter-branch' step was unnecessary and skipped safely — don't assume the reword step is always needed.

tee_key_state (used by TEE tombstone/republish e2e tests) is seeded by the API's TeeKeyStateService fetching the worker's pubkey at boot, not by the tee-worker itself — an empty table means the API's startup fetch failed, not that the worker is down.

Local dev stack: tee-worker's container port 3001 gets remapped to host :3002 because cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing already owns host :3001; TEE_WORKER_URL must be explicitly set to :3002 plus a matching TEE_WORKER_SECRET (Bearer auth) for the API to seed tee_key_state — otherwise it silently logs 'TEE worker unavailable' and 3 e2e tests fail with misleading 'tee_key_state is empty' errors.

resolveIpnsRecord maps HTTP 404→null but lets 410 fall through to throw (client.ts ~line 132); createAndPublishIpnsRecord's publish half was changed in phase 73 to catch 410 and return {success:false, tombstoned:true} instead of throwing.

The 68.2-coderabbit-hardening-backlog.md pending todo file is the running home for shared-nav/write-envelope hardening follow-ups — new related findings should be appended there rather than filed as new todo files.

code.finding: refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey reseeded publishedNode from cached getSharedFolderState() (stale) instead of re-resolving via IPNS; fixed to mirror the restoreToBreadcrumbIndex pattern (seed then getSdkClient().refreshSharedFolder) so a co-writer can recover after a stale-not-revoked write failure. Fix landed in commit 7e0026862.

publishedParent resolve was seeded from getSharedFolderState/publishedNode without checking sequence consistency against the independently-resolved children/seq, risking an older envelope being adopted; a seq-consistency guard mirroring doReresolveFolderInPlace was added during PR-review triage.

Test 20 (WRITE-04) asserted the pre-phase-73 throw-on-410 contract for createAndPublishIpnsRecord; updated to assert the new {success:false, tombstoned:true} return-value contract introduced by SC4, confirmed no production caller relied on the old throw behavior before changing the test.

workflow: Running independent gate checks (verify/secure/crypto-privacy/general-security agents, SDK E2E build+run, CodeRabbit CLI) fully in parallel/background while doing other work (diff review, memory writes) sped up the ship loop considerably.

Piped bash exit codes can mask a command's true exit status — a background task notification reported the SDK E2E run as exit 0, but the real exit was 1 (3 failing tests); always re-check actual test output/tail rather than trusting a summarized exit code.

When diagnosing 'test infra failure' vs 'real regression', systematically checking port mappings and auth secrets end-to-end (probing both candidate ports directly) resolved an otherwise confusing three-test failure quickly.
Before filing a new todo, grep/read existing pending todo files for an overlapping item and append/refine in place rather than creating a duplicate.

friction: A background task notification falsely reported the SDK E2E suite as exit code 0 when the actual exit was 1 (masked by a shell pipe), requiring a manual re-check of the tail output.

Diagnosing the 3 TEE e2e test failures required a long investigation chain (container status → DB tee_key_state → API init logs → port collision → auth secret mismatch) before confirming it was a local-stack config gap unrelated to phase 73's code.
CodeRabbit's PR-level review included hallucinated cross-references to nonexistent phases (45-55/79-88) in doc-nit findings, adding noise that had to be identified and discarded.
gh CLI calls hit a transient network timeout requiring a retry before pushing/creating the PR.

The task's step 7 (conventional-commit reword via git filter-branch) assumed commits needed rewriting, but they were already conventional — required verification before skipping to avoid unnecessary risky history rewriting.
open_items: Greptile's in-flight descent race finding (useSharedNavigationActions.ts:419) was judged real but risky to fix at ship time — logged as a new item in the 68.2-coderabbit-hardening-backlog.md todo rather than fixed now.
Ungated publishedParent write-base resolve (client.ts:5674) — the seq-consistency guard was applied, but the broader defense-in-depth follow-up remains tracked in the 68.2 hardening backlog (item 4).

Session transcript ends mid-flow: PR #603's review threads (8 total, mix of CodeRabbit/Greptile findings) were only partially triaged/resolved — final push, thread resolution confirmation (N/N), and final CI/status report were not yet completed.
TEE-worker local port-collision + auth-secret gotcha was saved to persistent memory for future sessions.
